cluster_name: Unusually powerful nor'easter batters US Northeast with flooding and outages
tldr: Across 18 headlines from 15 outlets, the dominant advertised frame is infrastructure disruption — power outages and flight cancellations — appearing in roughly half of all titles. The death toll surfaces explicitly in only four headlines (Le Parisien, Malay Mail, NDTV, and a Hindustan Times piece), a narrower callout than body coverage sustains. Strikingly, the 'rare for the season' climatological framing — a near-universal editorial hook in body text — is confined to just two French titles at the headline layer, suggesting the anomaly was amplified in body copy but suppressed at the homepage.
event_summary: A powerful nor'easter struck the northeastern US on September 26-27, 2026, causing flooding, power outages, and over 400 flight cancellations, killing at least one person. New York and New Jersey declared emergencies as tens of millions from Maine to Virginia faced dangerous conditions.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Sole headline in the corpus focused exclusively on power outages with no mention of flooding, deaths, or emergency declarations — the most stripped-down infrastructure angle and the only US outlet headline that omits all human-cost language.

Only outlet to foreground the emergency declaration as the headline hook ('New York and New Jersey declare emergency'), making the governmental response the visible story at the homepage layer rather than the storm's physical effects.

Published a geographic tracker headline naming six specific US states — unique service-journalism framing in the corpus that treats the event as a real-time guidance resource for readers rather than a news dispatch.

One of only four outlets to embed the death toll in the headline itself; uniquely structures the title as a listicle of damages ('inondations, un mort, coupures d'électricité'), foregrounding human cost alongside infrastructure failure in a single compressed frame.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, the nor'easter story is dominated by infrastructure failure — power and aviation — across the political spectrum, while the seasonal anomaly that unified body coverage internationally is confined to French-language titles; the human death toll appears in fewer than a quarter of headlines, suppressed at the homepage relative to its prominence in body text.
